decisions: D-B9A-01 — ONE RULE, so the next author does not have to guess which lever to pull. A row exists where the pinned model produces, for forms of one word, a raw lemma that is not that word's dictionary headword, and the row sends it to the headword. Its converse keeps the table small: where the raw lemma IS a headword the course could mean, there is no row and the curriculum declares the lemma the model produces instead. Three measured shapes fall out of it and all three get the same treatment, because they are one defect — one word, two raw lemmas, depending on position: (1) prenominal/apocopated adjectives (buen/buena/buenas/buenos -> bueno, gran -> grande, tercer -> tercero); (2) a sentence-initial capital re-tagged PROPN keeping the surface as the lemma (Días -> día, Noches -> noche, Tardes -> tarde, Gracias -> gracia, Media -> medio); (3) a bare one-word document over- or mis-singularising (paragua -> paraguas, cucharo -> cuchara, to -> tos). Shape 3 runs the other way round and is safe only because none of `paragua`, `cucharo`, `to` is a Spanish word — that clause IS the safety argument, and a row whose raw side is a word would fold that word into another ledger item. `primer` gets no row because `primer` -> `primero` already.

D-B9A-01a — what the adversarial review changed, recorded because the shape it caught is subtle. The first version handled `Cuchara`, `Media` and `Paraguas` with capitalised `forms:` entries while handling `días`/`noches`/`tardes` with table rows, which is two treatments of one measured shape. Under D-B9A-01 they are all table rows or all curriculum declarations, and a capitalised `forms:` entry is now refused at load: `Gracias` -> `gracias` but `gracias` -> `gracia`, so a capital discharges the gate for a lexeme no ordinary sentence can select. `forms:` is for real lowercase forms only (plurals, inflections); position artefacts belong in the table.

D-B9A-02 — reflexive infinitives, collapsing pronouns and `fuera` get NO row, and the measurement is why: `levantarse`, `levantarlo`, `levantarla`, `levantarle`, `levantarlos` and `levantarles` all produce the one raw lemma `levantar él`, and `fuera` produces `ser` because it is spelled like the imperfect subjunctive of ser/ir. A table cannot re-split what the lemmatiser merged, and a row `ser -> fuera` would claim every `era`/`fue` teaches the adverb. The curriculum stopped declaring those lemmas; `afuera` (measured self-lemmatising) carries the locative pair.

D-B9A-03 — the third column is measured with the BARE surface (`LEMMA_NORMALISATION_PROBE`), declared in config and covered by the digest. It is the bare surface because that is exactly the call `lemmatise_surface` takes, which is what the G2 frequency tail and the B9(c) gate both run; a carrier-sentence probe would be evidence about a call the pipeline never makes. Measured: `cuchara` alone -> `cucharo`, `cuchara` in a sentence -> `cuchara`, so the column means nothing without saying which.

D-B9C-01 — the reachability gate does NOT consult the G2 lexicon, though `solve` has it in hand. Lexicon membership is stronger evidence than a one-word document and that is the problem: it makes the verdict a property of the corpus, so the same curriculum and model would pass on one ingest and fail on the next, and a curriculum error could hide behind a lucky corpus. The gate is a pure function of (curriculum, pinned model, table), like the adapter self-test.

D-B9C-02 — no new validator id. The check runs inside the G3 stage, unconditionally and with no option to skip: VALIDATOR_IDS is what pack-ci's `pipeline-ready` job counts, so an unregistered id would skip both pack jobs green.

D-B9C-03 — a missing adapter is StageResult(ok=False) naming it, not a raise and never a skip. Ruling B14 settled the raise-vs-StageResult question for G7; the skip is the worse option, because `report.unreachable` left empty reads as 'nothing unreachable', which is how an unreachable lexeme got into the shipped curriculum in the first place. Pinned by test_INV_PACK_12_no_registered_adapter_fails_g3_by_name_and_never_skips_the_gate, which deliberately does not need the `nlp` group.

D-B9C-04 — unit 1's target ORDER is untouched and no lexeme was re-ordered anywhere; what changed in unit 1 is four unreachable removals, `gracias` -> `gracia`, and no `forms:`. Its ledger_digests move anyway, and NOT because of the curriculum: the B9(a) table puts `bueno` into the G2 lexicon, so unit 1's lesson deal gains a lemma at position 2. That is the blocker's option 2 arriving through the adapter rather than through the YAML, it is exactly what ruling B9(a) asks for, and it cannot be avoided while also fixing B9. The one-slot consequence in content/es/authoring/axis-fixture.jsonl is applied on this branch (see outOfLaneEditsApplied).

handoffs.gapfill: Unit 21 ('Walk someone through your morning') is the ONE digest-moving change in this commit, and it was forced: all 33 of its lexemes were reflexive infinitives, all 33 unreachable, and a unit with none left fails the loader. It now declares 12 base verbs (levantar, duchar, vestir, peinar, lavar, afeitar, acostar, despertar, sentar, poner, quitar, secar), all measured self-lemmatising and unclaimed elsewhere. Twelve keeps `derive_level_count` at 1 and the unit at 2 lessons, so course-global LESSON NUMBERING and every slot key are unchanged; what moves is `index.known` from unit 21 onward, so slots in units 21-30 get a new ledger_digest and their authored rows need a re-digest (not a re-authoring).
handoffs.gapfillSecond: The table itself also re-partitions the G2 lexicon — `buen`, `buena`, `buenas`, `buenos`, `días`, `noches`, `tardes`, `gran` and `tercer` stop being lexicon keys and their counts fold into the ledger lemma — so lexicon ranks shift and any unit that back-filled one of those loses it. Ruling B9 anticipates this: 're-key only rows whose ledger_digest changes'. The scale is not knowable from the adapter alone; it needs one `coursekit build es`.
handoffs.founder: Unit 1 still does not teach `llamar`, and 'Say hello and give your name' is the unit that should. Adding it would give unit 1 a target lemma it does not have today and move every unit-1 ledger_digest — which the brief reserves. Recorded here rather than done.

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: The third column of every normalisation row is RE-MEASURED against the RAW lemma by test_INV_PACK_06_every_declared_surface_really_produces_its_raw_lemma, through the adapter's `raw_lemma_of_surface`. The first version read `record['lemmas'][0]`, which is already normalised, so the comparison was circular and two rows (`días`, `tardes`) carried surfaces the model contradicts while the test stayed green. Column one of the table is now verified by something.

test_a_sentence_with_no_normalised_row_is_left_alone_by_the_table asserts every frozen sentence ABSENT from ADAPTER_SELFTEST_ES_NORMALISED normalises to its own raw fingerprint — so a new row that fires somewhere nobody looked fails the suite instead of quietly moving a lemma in a pack that is already built.

test_INV_PACK_40_every_row_is_well_formed_and_terminates refuses a row whose ledger lemma is another row's raw lemma. `ledger_lemma` makes exactly one pass, so a chain would leave the answer depending on dict order; it is refused by assertion rather than by a fixed-point loop, which would hide the mistake.

test_INV_PACK_40_the_lemma_normalisation_table_is_declared_in_exactly_one_place now greps the AST for NAMES IN CODE (import, bare reference, attribute) rather than the file's text, because g3_solve.py's docstring names the table to tell a reader where it lives and a text-level grep called that a second reader. A real second reader needs one of those three forms and cannot avoid all of them.

test_INV_PACK_06_a_declared_form_reaches_its_lexeme_mid_sentence_and_lowercase is the corroborating half of the gate: the gate probes a bare surface, which is unavoidably sentence-initial, so on its own it cannot tell `trabajos` -> `trabajo` from `Gracias` -> `gracias`. Measured over all 38 declared forms in five carriers, same answer in every one.
test_a_form_repeated_or_equal_to_the_lexeme_is_probed_once — `taught_forms` dedupes, so a lexeme named twice in target_lexemes cannot report the same attempt twice in the failure line.

outOfLaneEditsApplied.$comment: THREE FILES OUTSIDE this task's declared file lane are edited on this branch, and the integrator should know why before rebasing. All three are forced by deliverable (1) — the B9(a) table re-partitions the G2 lexicon, so artefacts that snapshot the old partition go stale — and NONE of them is touched by any of the four parallel P2 round-3 lanes (checked with `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` in each of the five worktrees on 2026-09-12), so there is no collision to resolve. The previous attempt deferred them and left the branch red: `uv run --group nlp pytest -q` was 4 FAILED + 16 ERROR here and EXIT=0 at origin/main b9a68eb, which pack-ci would have reported as this branch breaking the suite.
